title: Cain and Abel
summary: Anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin. This short lesson helps kids read, understand, and play through the passage.

read_it.prompt: Read Genesis 4:1-16 and look for how this passage teaches: Anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin.

tell_it: Cain became angry when his offering was not accepted. God warned him, but Cain chose jealousy and hurt his brother.
understand_it: Anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin. This lesson keeps the main point simple: God is faithful, His Word is true, and His people can respond with faith and obedience.
age_5_7_explanation: Cain and Abel reminds us that God is good and we can trust Him. Anger matters.
age_8_11_explanation: Cain and Abel shows that following God is not only knowing the story. It means learning this truth: Anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin.
teen_explanation: Cain and Abel gives older students room to think about faith under pressure. The passage teaches that anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin. It also asks how belief becomes action.
key_truths: Anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin.
God is faithful and His people can trust Him.
life_application: A kid can practice this when anger is needed: at school, with siblings, during disappointment, or when choosing between an easy wrong thing and a harder right thing.

quiz_questions.question: What did God warn Cain about?
choices: Sin was crouching at the door
quiz_questions.answer: Sin was crouching at the door
quiz_questions.explanation: The passage points us back to this answer: Sin was crouching at the door. It helps kids remember the main event and the truth it teaches.

quiz_questions.question: This lesson teaches that anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin.
quiz_questions.explanation: That is the plain lesson focus for this passage, stated in kid-friendly language.

memory_verse.prompt: Remember Genesis 4:7 as a short anchor for this lesson.

discussion_questions: What happened in Cain and Abel?
What does this passage teach us about God or following Him?
Where could this lesson help you at home, school, church, or with friends?

activity.title: Anger Thermometer
activity.instructions: Draw or act out the lesson scene, then name the one clear truth: Anger must be brought to God before it grows into sin.

prayer_prompt: Lord, help me learn from Cain and Abel. Teach me to trust You, listen to Your Word, and live this truth this week.
